headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection/cascading-error from AutoGPT consuming untrusted outputs; other pairwise risks are mostly low-to-medium due to limited shared surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT exposes filesystem and agent-protocol I/O plus shell/subprocess execution, so it can ingest and act on content from another agent. system_prompts_leaks is a source-available corpus about prompt leaks, so if its outputs are copied into AutoGPT, instruction hijacking is plausible. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF agent_b content is copied into agent_a's filesystem or agent protocol input, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF agent_a parses external text as instructions without provenance checks, attacker-controlled directives can steer execution.
mitigations: Restrict agent_a to a quarantined input folder.
Add a provenance header check before agent_a reads agent_b outputs.
Disable shell execution for runs that ingest external text.
Manually review any agent_b-derived prompt before passing it onward.

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT can touch the filesystem and make allowlisted network egress, but the profile shows no secrets handled and no shared workspace with agent_b. system_prompts_leaks has no I/O surfaces and no network egress, so direct leakage from the pair is not evidenced. The remaining pathway is limited and requires external setup, so low fits better than medium.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted on the same writable workspace, file contents can cross between them.
IF agent_a is given sensitive files through its filesystem surface, those files may be sent to allowlisted endpoints.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for the two agents.
Mount sensitive directories read-only or not at all.
Keep agent_a's allowlist limited to required endpoints.
Avoid placing secrets in any shared folder.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can write via filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while system_prompts_leaks has no declared write or network capabilities. There is no evidence that both agents concurrently modify the same mutable resource, so a true write-write conflict is not documented. Because AutoGPT's filesystem access is real and the other profile is sparse, the safest choice is low, not none.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory, AutoGPT can overwrite files used by the other workflow.
IF an external orchestrator gives both agents the same mutable resource, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: Assign distinct directories to each agent.
Serialize any shared file updates with a lock file.
Keep agent_b read-only in the workflow.
Run a quick dry-run to confirm no shared writes occur.

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate and act on outputs, and system_prompts_leaks is a prompt-leak corpus that could be treated as authoritative source material. If agent_a's text is fed into agent_b or vice versa without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions. No built-in verification or locking is documented, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF agent_b renders or republishes agent_a output without verification, mistakes propagate.
IF agent_a consumes agent_b text as facts, false claims can be operationalized.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before any action-taking.
Require citations for any factual claim passed between agents.
Use a schema validator on inter-agent messages.
Disable autonomous execution for the second hop.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are declared for either agent, and both profiles show empty touched-data fields. Without a documented compliance mismatch, a residency or retention violation is not evidenced. The other agent is not cited separately because the profiles do not expose any compliance-relevant distinction.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either agent's workflow, compliance review is required.
IF a deployment adds residency or retention constraints not present in the profiles, reassess the pair.
mitigations: Document the data classes before deployment.
Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Add a retention policy check to the workflow.
Review residency requirements if the deployment changes.
